title: Add try/catch around onSendAgain/onVerified in EmailVerificationConfirmPanel and un-skip the C6/E5 regression tests
rule: EH-2/EH-3 (typed exceptions handled at the boundary; no log-less catch) discovered via disclosed-but-unfixed test skips

evidence.quote:
// BUG: _wrapSendAgain uses try/finally but not try/catch, so exceptions
      // from onSendAgain propagate as unhandled async errors, crashing the

why: `_wrapSendAgain`/`_wrapVerified` use try/finally with no catch, so any exception from the injected callback propagates as an unhandled async error instead of a graceful error state. The onVerified callback built in sign_in_controller.dart's buildVerificationCallback calls _refreshAndCheckVerified -> authRepo.reloadCurrentUser() with no surrounding try/catch, so a transient network error while the user is mid email-verification is a real, reachable path to this unhandled exception -- not just a theoretical one. Both regression tests that would catch this (C6, E5) are disclosed but left skip:true with no Linear id, so the gap is invisible to anyone not reading test source.
recommendation: Add a catch clause to both wrapper methods that resets the loading flag and surfaces the failure (e.g. via a callback/snackbar, matching the pattern already used for signOut() failures elsewhere in this feature), then remove skip: true from C6 and E5.
acceptance_criteria: _wrapSendAgain and _wrapVerified catch and handle exceptions from the injected callbacks (no bare try/finally).
C6 and E5 in email_verification_confirm_panel_test.dart run (skip: true removed) and pass.

corrections: EH-2/EH-3 rule-fit is a bit loose (no catch clause exists to call 'empty/log-less'; EH-2 is about layer-boundary conversion) but the underlying defect and reachability are independently confirmed.
